title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Playbook
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Overview

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's standard processes for hiring, candidate evaluation, employee onboarding (0-90 days), and the quarterly/annual performance & feedback cycle. It is intended for hiring managers, interviewers, people-ops partners, and new managers running reviews. Follow these procedures unless an exception is approved by People Ops.

Goals
- Reduce time-to-hire while maintaining high quality of hire.
- Deliver a consistent, delighting new hire experience that accelerates time-to-productivity.
- Standardize performance conversations and calibration across teams.

Owners & Contacts
- Primary owner: People Ops (people-ops@redwood-example.com)
- Hiring process questions: Recruiting team (recruiting@redwood-example.com)
- Manager coaching and calibration: People Ops & Talent Partners

1) Hiring process (high level)

Summary: We use a structured, interviewer-led process with clear scorecards and a certified interviewer requirement for IC and manager hires. Typical stages and target SLAs are listed below.

Typical stages (stage — typical duration — owner):
| Stage | Target duration | Owner | Description |
|-------|-----------------|-------|-------------|
| Requisition approval | 1-3 business days | Hiring manager & Finance | Create req in Greenhouse with role profile, compensation band, and interview panel.
| Sourcing & screening | 3-14 business days | Recruiting | Screen resumes, run phone/virtual screen (30 min).
| Technical / role interviews | 7-14 business days | Hiring team | 2-4 interviews depending on role: technical, system design, coding/work sample, cross-functional partner.
| Hiring committee & calibration | 3-7 business days | Hiring manager & People Ops | Evidence review and committee sign-off for manager/level 5+ roles.
| Offer & negotiation | 1-7 business days | Hiring manager & Recruiting | Send verbal then written offer. Work with People Ops for approvals.
| Acceptance to start | varies | Recruiting & Hiring manager | Coordinate start date, relocation/onboarding as needed.

Stage details and rules:
- Requisition: All roles must have a completed scorecard (competencies and success metrics), a compensation band, and a hiring manager with an identified interview panel before posting.
- Interviewer certification: All interviewers must complete Redwood Interviewer Training and pass the short quiz every 12 months. Compliance is tracked in the recruiting LMS.
- Interview feedback: Use Greenhouse unified scorecard. Feedback should be entered within 48 hours of the interview.
- Candidate diversity: Use diverse-slate target (minimum 30% diverse slate) for senior roles (L4+) and hard-to-fill roles.

Scorecard guidance (what to evaluate)
- Core competency anchors: Ownership, Technical Craft, Communication, Problem Solving, Culture Add.
- Each competency: rate 1-5 and add evidence (objective examples).
- Hiring decision should reference the scorecard evidence, not impressions.

2) Interview formats and sample templates

Phone/Screen (30 minutes)
- Purpose: Validate interest, culture fit, basic qualification, and logistical fit (compensation, eligibility).
- Agenda: 5m intros, 10m background & projects, 10m role fit & expectations, 5m questions + next steps.

Technical Interview (60 minutes)
- Purpose: Assess role-specific skills and problem solving at the target level.
- Agenda: 5m intro, 40-45m problem or design exercise, 10m debrief + questions.
- Grading rubric: correctness, approach, communication, trade-off awareness.

Work-sample / Take-home
- Use sparingly for senior IC roles and design-heavy positions. Timebox at 3-6 hours and provide clear acceptance criteria. Offer paid take-home where >6 hours.

Offer templates (example snippet)
- Subject: Offer — [Candidate Name] — [Role] at Redwood Inference
- Body (high level): Role title, level, reporting manager, base salary, equity grant summary, target start date, link to full offer letter (PDF).

3) Onboarding: 0-90 day plan

Principles
- First 7 days: orientation & core access. First 30 days: learning & contribution. First 90 days: independent, measurable impact.
- Clear owner for each onboarding task: Recruiting for pre-boarding, Manager for role-specific ramp, People Ops for policy & benefits.

Pre-boarding (before day 1)
- Tasks (Recruiter): send welcome packet, benefits enrollment instructions, equipment survey, and first-week agenda.
- IT & Security tasks: create account, SSO, grant core tool access (Slack, Google Workspace, JIRA, internal Confluence), assign laptop and VPN credentials.

Day 1-7: Orientation
- Manager checklist:
  1. Welcome meeting and team intro + org chart overview.
  2. Review 30/60/90 goals and expected deliverables.
  3. Set calendar blocks for training and shadow sessions.
  4. Assign a peer buddy with a clear 30-day pairing plan.
- People Ops checklist:
  - Benefits orientation, payroll enrollment, compliance training links.
  - New hire paperwork complete.

First 30 days: Learning & initial contributions
- Goals: Complete required training, have first feature/bug fix or contribution, and attend cross-functional onboarding sessions.
- Manager actions: weekly 1:1, explicit feedback each week, demo/knowledge-sharing session at week 4.

30-90 days: Ownership & performance checkpoint
- 30-day check-in: manager to document progress vs 30-day goals and submit summary to People Ops.
- 60-day mentor review: buddy and manager discuss integration and blockers.
- 90-day review: formal manager evaluation and reciprocal feedback. Outcome: continue, adjust plan, or initiate development plan.

Onboarding checklist (table)
| Category | Owner | Completion target | Example items |
|---------|-------|------------------|---------------|
| Accounts & Access | IT/Security | Day 1 | SSO, Slack, VPN, GitHub access |
| HR & Payroll | People Ops | Day 3 | Benefits enrollment, tax forms |
| Team ramp | Manager | Week 1-4 | 30/60/90 goals, buddy pairing, codebase walkthroughs |
| Compliance & Security | People Ops | Day 7 | Mandatory trainings (security, privacy) |

4) Performance & feedback cycle

Cadence
- Ongoing: Continuous feedback encouraged; managers should document coaching notes in 1:1s.
- Quarterly: Check-ins (informal) between manager and direct reports.
- Annual: Formal performance review with calibration and compensation cycle.

Review components
- Self-assessment: Employee completes a 1-2 page self-assessment aligned to role-level competencies.
- Manager assessment: Written summary with examples for each competency and level.
- Peer feedback: 3-5 peers provide short structured feedback.
- Calibration: Managers meet in a compensation calibration panel to align leveling and compensation decisions.

Timeline (example for engineering teams)
1. Performance window: Jan 1 – Dec 31
2. Self-assessments open: Jan 5 – Jan 20
3. Manager reviews & peer feedback: Jan 21 – Feb 10
4. Calibration meetings: Feb 15 – Feb 28
5. Compensation letters & ratings communicated: Mar 5 – Mar 12

Rating guidance and calibration
- Levels are calibrated to competency anchors (IC1-IC5, M1-M3). Do not rely solely on output volume — emphasize impact, complexity, and scope.
- Calibration panels review evidence and manager narratives. People Ops may escalate inconsistent ratings for re-review.

Performance improvement and development
- Low performance: Manager should provide documented coaching and a Clear Performance Plan (CPP) with measurable milestones and a 30-90 day timeline. People Ops must be engaged before issuing a formal CPP.
- High performance: Managers should discuss promotion readiness and roadmap for acceleration. Nominate for spot awards and consider stretch assignments.

5) Manager guide: giving feedback, hiring responsibly, and running reviews

Giving feedback
- Frequency: Aim for weekly 1:1s and ad-hoc feedback within 48 hours of the observed behavior.
- Framework: Use Situation-Behavior-Impact (SBI) to make feedback specific and actionable.
- Balance: Deliver strengths + area for improvement; end with a clear next step.

Hiring as a manager
- Before opening a req: define role outcomes, success metrics for 6 months, interview scorecard, and compensation band.
- Interviewing: Use the scorecard, document objective evidence, and avoid questions outside role scope (e.g., compensation history).

Running reviews and calibration
- Evidence-first: Provide concrete examples tied to competencies.
- Peer feedback: Collect structured peer feedback; anonymize during calibration.
- Calibration panels: Bring leveling rationale and comparable role examples. People Ops will provide historical compensation bands to inform decisions.

Templates & artifacts (copyable)
- 30/60/90 goal template (example):
  - 30-day: Learn codebase, ship first small fix, meet key partners.
  - 60-day: Deliver a small feature, own one service area, present a tech demo.
  - 90-day: Independently own a story from design to production and mentor a junior peer.

- Offer email (snippet):
  "Hi [Name],
  We are excited to offer you the role of [Title] at Redwood Inference. The proposed base salary is $[X], with a target equity grant described in the enclosed letter. Please find the full offer attached. We look forward to your response by [date]."

- 90-day review checklist (manager):
  1. Review 30/60/90 documented goals.
  2. Document performance examples and rating.
  3. Solicit feedback from buddy and 2-3 peers.
  4. Meet with employee to discuss outcome and next steps.
  5. Share summary with People Ops.

6) Special cases and exceptions

Hiring from competitors: Escalate to Legal for approval when hiring from regulated customers or critical partners.
Visa sponsorship & relocation: Engage People Ops and Finance early; factor 6-12 weeks for work authorization where applicable.
Contractors & vendors: Use procurement-approved MSAs and execute statement of work (SoW) before engagement.

7) Metrics & continuous improvement

Key metrics we track
- Time-to-fill (requisition approval -> offer acceptance), target: 30 days median.
- Time-to-productivity (start -> first independent PR/feature), target: 60 days median.
- Offer acceptance rate, target: >= 65%.
- New hire 90-day retention, target: >= 95%.

Process improvement loop
- Quarterly People Ops review meeting to inspect metrics, run retros with hiring managers, and iterate on the scorecard and interview materials.
- Run an annual interviewer calibration workshop and refresh the interviewer training content.

Appendices
- Links: Recruiting playbook, Greenhouse templates, Offer letter library, Interviewer training deck.
- Glossary: IC = Individual Contributor, M = Manager, CPP = Clear Performance Plan, SSO = Single Sign-On.
